units.zh: 辛術 元文遙 趙彥深
units.en: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen
units.literal: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen

units.zh: 辛術，字懷哲，少明敏，有識度。
units.en: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, was clever and perceptive from boyhood, with a steady sense of what mattered.
units.literal: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, from youth was bright and keen, with judgment and discernment.

units.zh: 解褐司空胄曹參軍，與僕射高隆之共典營構鄴都宮室，術有思理，百工克濟。
units.en: His first appointment was staff member in the registrar's office of the directorate of works; with vice director Gao Longzhi he directed the building of Ye's palaces. Shu planned well, and every trade met its mark.
units.literal: Upon first office he was Staff Member in the Registrar's Office of the Directorate of Works; together with Vice Director Gao Longzhi he oversaw the construction of Ye's palaces—Shu had thoughtful designs, and all the crafts were brought to completion.

units.zh: 再遷尚書右丞。
units.en: He was promoted again to right vice director of the masters of writing.
units.literal: He was promoted again to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 出為清河太守，政有能名。
units.en: Sent out as administrator of Qinghe, he earned a name for capable rule.
units.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Qinghe; his governance won a reputation for ability.

units.zh: 追授幷州長史，遭父憂去職。
units.en: He was retroactively made chief clerk of Bing province, then left office to mourn his father.
units.literal: Retroactively appointed Chief Clerk of Bing province; he left office on father's mourning.

units.zh: 清河父老數百人詣闕請立碑頌德。
units.en: Several hundred Qinghe elders went to court to ask that a stele be raised in praise of his virtue.
units.literal: Several hundred elders of Qinghe went to the capital to request a stele praising his virtue.

units.zh: 文襄嗣事，與尚書左丞宋遊道、中書侍郎李繪等並追詣晉陽，俱為上客。
units.en: When Gao Cheng assumed power, he went with left vice director Song Youdao, secretariat attendant Li Hui, and others to Jinyang and was received as an honored guest.
units.literal: When Gao Cheng took up the succession, together with Left Vice Director Song Youdao, Secretariat Attendant Li Hui, and others he hurried to Jinyang; all became honored guests.

units.zh: 累遷散騎常侍。
units.en: He rose through repeated promotions to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

units.zh: 武定八年，侯景叛，除東南道行臺尚書，封江夏縣男，與高岳等破侯景，擒蕭明。
units.en: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled. Shu was made masters of writing on the southeastern mobile grand secretariat and enfeoffed as nan (baron) of Jiangxia county. With Gao Yue and others he broke Hou Jing and took Xiao Ming prisoner.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled; Shu was appointed Masters of Writing on the Southeastern Circuit Mobile Grand Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangxia county (male), and with Gao Yue and others defeated Hou Jing and captured Xiao Ming.

units.zh: 遷東徐州刺史，為淮南經略使。
units.en: He was transferred to governor of Eastern Xuzhou and made commissioner for Huainan pacification.
units.literal: Transferred to Governor of Eastern Xuzhou; made Commissioner for the Pacification of Huainan.

units.zh: 齊天保元年，侯景徵江西租稅，術率諸軍渡淮斷之，燒其稻數百萬石。
units.en: In Qi's first Tianbao year, Hou Jing levied rents from Jiangxi. Shu led troops across the Huai to block him and burned several million shi of his grain.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianbao of Qi, Hou Jing levied rents and taxes from Jiangxi; Shu led the armies across the Huai to cut it off and burned several million shi of his rice.

units.zh: 還鎮下邳，人隨術北渡淮者三千餘家。
units.en: When he returned to garrison Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed him north across the Huai.
units.literal: Returning to garrison at Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed Shu north across the Huai.

units.zh: 東徐州刺史郭誌殺郡守。
units.en: Guo Zhi, governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed his commandery administrator.
units.literal: Guo Zhi, Governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed the commandery administrator.

units.zh: 文宣聞之，勑術自今所統十餘州地諸有犯法者，刺史先啟聽報，以下先斷後表聞。
units.en: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu that in the dozen-odd provinces under him, whenever anyone broke the law the governor must first report and wait for word; lower officials might decide first and memorialize later.
units.literal: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu: from now on in the more than ten provinces under his command, wherever anyone violated the law, the governor should first report and await instruction; subordinates might judge first and memorialize afterward.

units.zh: 齊代行臺兼總人事，自術始也。
units.en: In Qi the practice of a mobile grand secretariat also holding personnel authority began with Shu.
units.literal: In Qi, a mobile grand secretariat concurrently overseeing personnel matters began with Shu.

units.zh: 安州刺史、臨清太守、盱眙蘄城二鎮將犯法，術皆案奏殺之。
units.en: The governor of Anzhou, the administrator of Linqing, and the garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all committed capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them put to death.
units.literal: The Governor of Anzhou, Administrator of Linqing, and the two garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all violated capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them executed.

units.zh: 睢州刺史及所部郡守俱犯大辟，朝廷以其奴婢百口及資財盡賜術，三辭不見許，術乃送詣所司，不復以聞。
units.en: The governor of Suizhou and every commandery administrator under him faced capital punishment. The court granted Shu all their slaves—more than a hundred households—and their property. He declined three times and was refused; Shu then turned everything over to the proper office and did not keep it.
units.literal: The Governor of Suizhou and all the commandery administrators under him committed capital offenses; the court granted Shu all their hundred-odd slaves and entire assets; he declined three times but was not permitted; Shu then sent them to the relevant office and no longer kept them for himself.

units.zh: 邢卲聞之，遺術書曰：「昔鐘離意云『孔子忍渴於盜泉』，便以珠璣委地，足下今能如此，可謂異代一時。」
units.en: Xing Shao heard and wrote Shu: "Long ago Zhongli Yi said that Confucius would endure thirst rather than drink from Robber Spring, and so cast pearls and jade aside; you, sir, can do as much today—truly one moment in another age."
units.literal: Xing Shao heard of it and sent Shu a letter, saying: "In antiquity Zhongli Yi said, 'Confucius bore thirst at Robber Spring,' and thereby cast pearls and jades to the ground; you, sir, can do the same today—one may call it the same moment across different ages."

units.zh: 及王僧辯破侯景，術招攜安撫，城鎮相繼款附，前後二十餘州。
units.en: When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu won men over and pacified the land; towns and garrisons submitted one after another—more than twenty provinces in all.
units.literal: When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu recruited and pacified; cities and garrisons in succession submitted; in all more than twenty provinces.

units.zh: 於是移鎮廣陵。
units.en: He then shifted his headquarters to Guangling.
units.literal: Thereupon he moved his command to Guangling.

units.zh: 獲傳國璽送鄴，文宣以璽告於太廟。
units.en: He recovered the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang presented it at the imperial ancestral temple.
units.literal: He obtained the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang reported the seal at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 此璽卽秦所制，方四寸，上紐交盤龍，其文曰：「受命于天，旣壽永昌。」
units.en: This was the seal Qin had made: four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons. Its inscription read, "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity."
units.literal: This seal was that made by Qin, four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons; its inscription read: "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity."

units.zh: 二漢相傳，又傳魏、晉。
units.en: The two Han dynasties passed it down; Wei and Jin passed it down as well.
units.literal: The Two Han transmitted it; it was also transmitted through Wei and Jin.

units.zh: 懷帝敗，沒於劉聰。
units.en: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost to Liu Cong.
units.literal: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost among Liu Cong.

units.zh: 聰敗，沒於石氏。
units.en: When Cong fell, it passed to the Shi clan.
units.literal: When Cong was defeated, it was lost among the Shi clan.

units.zh: 石氏敗，晉穆帝永和中，濮陽太守戴僧施得之，遣督護何融送于建鄴。
units.en: When the Shi fell, in the Yonghe reign of Jin's Emperor Mu, Dai Sengshi, administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.
units.literal: When the Shi clan was defeated, in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, Dai Sengshi, Administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent Supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.

units.zh: 歷宋、齊、梁，梁敗，侯景得之。
units.en: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing took it.
units.literal: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing obtained it.

units.zh: 景敗，侍中趙思賢以璽投景南兗州刺史郭元建，送于術，故術以進焉。
units.en: When Jing was defeated, attendant-in-ordinary Zhao Sixian gave the seal to Jing's southern Yanzhou governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; thus Shu was able to present it.
units.literal: When Jing was defeated, Attendant Zhong Zhao Sixian cast the seal upon Jing's Southern Yanzhou Governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; therefore Shu presented it.

units.zh: 尋徵為殿中尚書，領太常卿，仍與朝賢議定律令。
units.en: He was soon summoned as palace masters of writing and director of the imperial ancestral temple, and still joined court worthies in revising laws and ordinances.
units.literal: Soon summoned as Masters of Writing in the Palace, leading Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and still deliberated on laws and ordinances with court worthies.

units.zh: 遷吏部尚書，食南兗州梁郡幹。
units.en: He was promoted to director of personnel and drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in southern Yanzhou.
units.literal: Promoted to Director of Personnel; drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in Southern Yanzhou.

units.zh: 遷鄴以後，大選之職，知名者數四，互有得失，未能盡美。
units.en: After the court moved to Ye, four famous men held the great selection office in turn; each had strengths and flaws, and none achieved perfection.
units.literal: After the move to Ye, the great selection posts had four well-known holders, each with gain and loss, none attaining perfection.

units.zh: 文襄帝少年高朗，所弊者疏；
units.en: Gao Cheng in his youth was bright and open; his fault was looseness.
units.literal: Gao Cheng in his youth was lofty and clear; what harmed him was laxity.

units.zh: 袁叔德沉密謹厚，所傷者細；
units.en: Yuan Shude was grave, careful, and thorough; his fault was excessive detail.
units.literal: Yuan Shude was deep, close, and cautious; what harmed him was minuteness.

units.zh: 楊愔風流辨給，取士失於浮華。
units.en: Yang Yin was eloquent and quick; in choosing men he favored show over substance.
units.literal: Yang Yin was polished and quick in debate; in selecting men he erred toward flashiness.

units.zh: 唯術性尚貞明，取士以才器，循名責實，新舊參舉，管庫必擢，門閥不遺。
units.en: Only Shu, upright by nature, chose by talent and office, matched names to reality, mixed veterans and newcomers, promoted men from the storehouses, and did not overlook great families.
units.literal: Only Shu, by nature upright and clear, chose men by talent and capacity, held names to facts, mixed old and new in nomination, must promote from storehouses, and did not leave out noble houses.

units.zh: 考之前後銓衡，在術最為折衷，甚為當時所稱舉。
units.en: Comparing earlier and later rounds of selection, Shu's was the most even-handed, and his age praised him highly.
units.literal: Reviewing selection before and after, Shu's was most balanced, and was greatly praised by the age.

units.zh: 天保末，文宣嘗令術選百員官，參選者二三千人，術題目士子，人無謗讟，其所旌擢，後亦皆致通顯。
units.en: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once ordered Shu to choose a hundred officials from two or three thousand candidates. Shu tested the scholars; no one murmured against him, and those he advanced later all rose to high rank.
units.literal: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once had Shu select a hundred officials; those who competed numbered two or three thousand; Shu examined the scholars; none slandered; those he honored and promoted later all attained high prominence.

units.zh: 術清儉，寡嗜欲。
units.en: Shu was austere and frugal, with few wants.
units.literal: Shu was pure and frugal, with few desires.

units.zh: 勤於所職，未嘗暫懈。
units.en: He was diligent in office and never slackened even for a moment.
units.literal: Diligent in his duties, never briefly slackening.

units.zh: 臨軍以威嚴，牧人有惠政。
units.en: Before the army he was stern; over the people he ruled with kindness.
units.literal: Facing armies with stern authority; governing the people with beneficent policy.

units.zh: 少愛文史，晚更修學，雖在戎旅，手不釋卷。
units.en: He loved letters in youth and studied harder in later years; even on campaign he never put down his books.
units.literal: In youth he loved literature and history; in later years he studied further; though on campaign, his hand never left the scroll.

units.zh: 及定淮南，凡諸資物一毫無犯，唯大收典籍，多是宋、齊、梁時佳本，鳩集萬餘卷，幷顧、陸之徒名畫、二王已下法書數亦不少，俱不上王府，唯入私門。
units.en: When Huainan was settled he took not a thread of booty, but gathered books in force—mostly fine Song, Qi, and Liang editions, more than ten thousand scrolls—along with celebrated paintings by Gu, Lu, and their circle and many works of calligraphy after the Two Wangs. None went to the imperial treasury; all entered his private house.
units.literal: When Huainan was pacified, of all goods he touched not a hairsbreadth; he only gathered books in great number—mostly fine editions from Song, Qi, and Liang times—more than ten thousand scrolls collected, together with famous paintings by Gu and Lu and their school, and calligraphies after the Two Wangs in no small number; none went to the imperial storehouse—only into his private gate.

units.zh: 及還朝，頗以饋遺權要，物議以此少之。
units.en: On returning to court he often sent gifts to the powerful, and opinion thought less of him for it.
units.literal: When he returned to court, he often gifted powerful figures; public opinion thereby thought less of him.

units.zh: 十年卒，年六十。
units.en: He died in the tenth year, at sixty.
units.literal: In the tenth year he died, age sixty.

units.zh: 皇建二年，贈開府儀同三司、中書監、青州刺史。
units.en: In the second year of Huangjian he was posthumously made grand mentor with ceremonies equal to the three excellencies, supervisor of the secretariat, and governor of Qingzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Huangjian, posthumously granted Grand Mentor with ceremonies equal to the Three Excellencies, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Governor of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 子閣卿，尚書郎。
units.en: His son Geqing served as a masters of writing lang.
units.literal: His son Geqing was a Masters of Writing lang.

units.zh: 閣卿弟衡卿，有識學，開府參軍事。
units.en: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing was learned and discerning and served as staff in a grand mentor's office.
units.literal: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing had judgment and learning; staff member in a grand mentor's office.

units.zh: 隋大業初，卒於太常丞。
units.en: Early in Sui's Daye reign he died as vice director of the imperial ancestral temple.
units.literal: Early in Daye of Sui, he died as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 元文遙，字德遠，河南洛陽人，魏昭成皇帝六世孫也。
units.en: Yuan Wenyao, styled Deyuan, was from Luoyang in Henan commandery, a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
units.literal: Yuan Wenyao, styled Deyuan, a man of Luoyang in Henan; sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

units.zh: 五世祖常山王遵。
units.en: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Changshan, Zun.
units.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Changshan, Zun.

units.zh: 父晞，有孝行，父卒，廬於墓側而終。
units.en: His father Xi was famed for filial piety; when his own father died, he lived by the tomb until he died there.
units.literal: His father Xi had filial conduct; when his father died, he dwelt by the tomb until he died himself.

units.zh: 文遙貴，贈特進、開府儀同三司、中書監，諡曰孝。
units.en: When Wenyao rose high, Xi was posthumously made special advancement, grand mentor equal to the three excellencies, and supervisor of the secretariat, with the posthumous name Filial.
units.literal: When Wenyao rose high, Xi was posthumously granted Special Advancement, Grand Mentor equal to Three Excellencies, Supervisor of Secretariat, posthumous name Xiao (Filial).

units.zh: 文遙敏慧夙成，濟陰王暉業每云：「此子王佐才也。」
units.en: Wenyao was clever from childhood. The prince of Jiyin, Huiye, often said, "This child has the makings of a king's helper."
units.literal: Wenyao from youth was keen and clever; Prince of Jiyin Huiye often said: "This boy is talent for assisting a king."

units.zh: 暉業嘗大會賓客，有人將《何遜集》初入洛，諸賢皆贊賞之。
units.en: Once Huiye held a great gathering of guests. Someone brought He Xun's collected works, newly arrived in Luoyang, and every worthy present praised them.
units.literal: Huiye once gathered guests in great assembly; someone brought the Collected Works of He Xun newly into Luoyang; all the worthies praised it.

units.zh: 河間邢卲試命文遙：「誦之幾遍可得？」
units.en: Xing Shao of Hejian tested Wenyao: "Recite it—how many readings before you can?"
units.literal: Xing Shao of Hejian tested Wenyao: "Recite it—how many times through before you can?"

units.zh: 文遙一覽便誦，時年十餘歲。
units.en: Wenyao read it once and recited it; he was barely past ten.
units.literal: Wenyao read once and recited; he was then just over ten.

units.zh: 濟陰王曰：「我家千里駒，今定如何？」
units.en: The prince of Jiyin said, "My house's thousand-li colt—what has he become?"
units.literal: The Prince of Jiyin said: "My house's thousand-li colt—what is he now?"

units.zh: 邢云：「此殆古來未有。」
units.en: Xing said, "This is probably unmatched since antiquity."
units.literal: Xing said: "This is probably without precedent since antiquity."

units.zh: 起家員外散騎常侍。
units.en: He began office as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, outside the regular quota.
units.literal: His first office was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, outside the regular quota.

units.zh: 遭父喪，服闋，除太尉東閤祭酒。
units.en: After his father's death and mourning, he was made libationer in the eastern pavilion of the grand marshal.
units.literal: He suffered father's mourning; when mourning ended, made Libationer in the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 以天下方亂，遂解官侍養，隱於林慮山。
units.en: With the realm in turmoil, he resigned to care for his mother and lived in seclusion on Mount Linlü.
units.literal: As the realm was in turmoil, he resigned office to tend his mother and hid on Mount Linlü.

units.zh: 武定中，文襄徵為大將軍府功曹。
units.en: In the Wuding era Gao Cheng summoned him as staff officer in the grand general's office.
units.literal: In Wuding, Gao Cheng summoned him as Staff Officer of the Grand General's government office.

units.zh: 齊受禪，於登壇所受中書舍人，宣傳文武號令。
units.en: When Qi received the mandate, at the enthronement altar he was made secretariat drafting officer and proclaimed civil and military orders.
units.literal: When Qi received the mandate, at the altar of enthronement he received the post of Secretariat Drafting Officer, proclaiming civil and military orders.

units.zh: 楊遵彥每云：「堪解穰侯印者，必在斯人。」
units.en: Yang Zunyian often said, "The man who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this one."
units.literal: Yang Zunyian often said: "He who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this man."

units.zh: 後忽被中旨幽執，竟不知所由。
units.en: Later he was suddenly seized on a secret imperial order; in the end no one knew why.
units.literal: Later he was suddenly imprisoned by secret imperial order, and in the end none knew the reason.

units.zh: 如此積年。
units.en: He remained so for many years.
units.literal: Thus for many years.

units.zh: 文宣後自幸禁獄，執手愧謝，親解所著金帶及御服賜之，卽日起為尚書祠部郎中。
units.en: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in apology, removed his own gold belt and court robes to give him, and that same day made him lang in the sacrificial affairs section of the masters of writing.
units.literal: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in ashamed apology, personally removed his gold belt and imperial robes and bestowed them, and that same day raised him to Lang in the Sacrificial Affairs section of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 孝昭攝政，除大丞相府功曹參軍，典機密。
units.en: When Gao Yan acted as regent, Wenyao was made staff officer in the grand chancellor's office and handled confidential matters.
units.literal: When Gao Yan acted as regent, appointed Staff Officer in the Grand Chancellor's government office, overseeing secrets.

units.zh: 及踐祚，除中書侍郎，封永樂縣伯，參軍國大事。
units.en: When Gao Yan took the throne, Wenyao was made secretariat attendant, enfeoffed as baron of Yongle county, and took part in great affairs of state.
units.literal: When he ascended the throne, made Secretariat Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Yongle county, and deliberated on great affairs of state.

units.zh: 及帝大漸，與平秦王歸彥、趙郡王叡等同受顧託，迎立武成。
units.en: When the emperor was near death, he and Prince of Pingqin Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others received the final charge and installed Gao Zhan.
units.literal: When the emperor was gravely ill, together with Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others he received final charge and welcomed Gao Zhan to the throne.

units.zh: 卽位，任遇轉隆，歷給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、侍中、中書監。
units.en: After Gao Zhan took the throne, Wenyao's favor rose still higher. He served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, chamberlain for attendants, and supervisor of the secretariat.
units.literal: Upon enthronement his favor grew ever higher; he passed through Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Chamberlain for Attendants, Supervisor of Secretariat.

units.zh: 天統二年，詔特賜姓高氏，籍屬宗正，子弟依例歲時入朝。
units.en: In the second year of Tiantong an edict specially granted him the surname Gao, registered him with the director of the imperial clan, and allowed his sons and younger brothers to attend seasonal court audiences by regulation.
units.literal: In the second year of Tiantong, an edict specially granted the surname Gao; registration placed under the Director of Imperial Clan; sons and younger brothers per regulation attended court at the seasons.

units.zh: 再遷尚書左僕射，進封寧都郡公、侍中。
units.en: He was promoted again to left vice director of the masters of writing and advanced to duke of Ningdu commandery while retaining the post of chamberlain for attendants.
units.literal: Promoted again to Left Vice Director of Masters of Writing; advanced to Duke of Ningdu commandery, still chamberlain for attendants.

units.zh: 文遙歷事三主，明達世務，每臨軒，多命宣勑，號令文武，聲韻高朗，發吐無滯。
units.en: Wenyao served three sovereigns and knew the affairs of the age. Whenever he faced the throne he was often ordered to proclaim edicts; his voice rang clear, and he delivered civil and military orders without stumbling.
units.literal: Wenyao served three sovereigns, clear in worldly affairs; whenever he faced the throne he was often ordered to proclaim edicts; his civil and military orders rang high and clear, delivered without hindrance.

units.zh: 然探測上旨，時有委巷之言，故不為知音所重。
units.en: Yet in reading the sovereign's mind he sometimes used coarse speech, and men of discernment did not esteem him highly.
units.literal: Yet probing the sovereign's intent, he sometimes had alley language, and so was not greatly valued by those who understood.

units.zh: 齊因魏朝，宰縣多用廝濫，至於士流恥居百里。
units.en: Qi followed Wei in making county magistrates too often from lowborn men, until gentlemen were ashamed to govern a hundred-li district.
units.literal: Qi inherited Wei; county magistrates were often base appointees, until gentlemen would be ashamed to hold a hundred-li post.

units.zh: 文遙以縣令為字人之切，遂請革選。
units.en: Wenyao held that the magistrate was the hinge of caring for the people and asked to reform how they were chosen.
units.literal: Wenyao held that the magistrate was crucial to caring for the people, and so requested reform of selection.

units.zh: 於是密令搜揚貴遊子弟，發勑用之。
units.en: Secret orders then sought out sons of great houses, and edicts put them in office.
units.literal: Thereupon secret orders searched out noble scions; edicts issued to employ them.

units.zh: 猶恐其披訴，總召集神武門，令趙郡王叡宣旨唱名，厚加慰喻。
units.en: Still fearing they would appeal, he gathered them all at Shenwu Gate and had Prince of Zhao Jun Rui read the edict, call each name, and speak words of comfort.
units.literal: Still fearing their appeals and complaints, all were summoned at the Shenwu Gate; Prince of Zhao Jun Rui was ordered to proclaim names and offer words of thick consolation.

units.zh: 士人為縣，自此始也。
units.en: From this gentlemen began to serve as county magistrates.
units.literal: Gentlemen serving as county magistrates began from this.

units.zh: 旣與趙彥深、和士開同被任遇，雖不如彥深清貞守道，又不為士開貪淫亂政，在於季、孟之間。
units.en: He shared favor with Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai. He was not so pure and steadfast as Yanshen, nor so greedy and corrupt as Shikai, but stood between them.
units.literal: As he shared favor with Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai, though he was not like Yanshen in purity and holding the Way, nor like Shikai in greedy debauchery and disordering government, he stood between the second and third.

units.zh: 然性和厚，與物無競，故時論不在彥深之下。
units.en: Yet he was mild and easy by nature and did not contend with others, and opinion did not place him below Yanshen.
units.literal: Yet his nature was genial and thick, without contention with others, and so contemporary opinion did not rank him below Yanshen.

units.zh: 初，文遙自洛遷鄴，惟有地十頃，家貧，所資衣食而已。
units.en: When Wenyao first moved from Luoyang to Ye he had only ten qing of land; the household was poor and had barely enough to eat and wear.
units.literal: At first, when Wenyao moved from Luoyang to Ye, he had only ten qing of land; the family was poor—enough only for food and clothing.

units.zh: 魏之將季，宗姓被侮，有人冒相侵奪，文遙卽以與之。
units.en: As Wei neared its fall, clan members were bullied. Someone seized his land by force; Wenyao at once yielded it.
units.literal: As Wei neared its end, clan names were insulted; someone falsely seized and encroached; Wenyao at once yielded it to him.

units.zh: 及貴，此人尚在，乃將家逃竄。
units.en: When Wenyao rose high, that man was still alive and fled with his family.
units.literal: When he rose high, that man was still alive and fled with his household.

units.zh: 文遙大驚，追加慰撫，還以與之。
units.en: Wenyao was alarmed, sent after him with reassurances, and again offered him the land.
units.literal: Wenyao was greatly alarmed, pursued him with comfort, and again yielded it.

units.zh: 彼人愧而不受，彼此俱讓，遂為閑田。
units.en: The man was ashamed and would not take it; each insisted on yielding, and the field lay fallow.
units.literal: The other man was ashamed and would not accept; each yielded to the other, and it became idle land.

units.zh: 至後主嗣位，趙郡王叡、婁定遠等謀出和士開，文遙亦參其議。
units.en: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, Lou Dingyuan, and others plotted to remove He Shikai; Wenyao joined the plot.
units.literal: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Prince Zhao Jun Rui, Lou Dingyuan, and others plotted to remove He Shikai; Wenyao also joined the deliberation.

units.zh: 叡見殺，文遙由是出為西兗州刺史。
units.en: Rui was killed, and Wenyao was sent out as governor of western Yanzhou.
units.literal: Rui was killed; Wenyao thereby went out as Governor of Western Yanzhou.

units.zh: 詣士開別，士開曰：「處得言地，使元家兒作令仆，深愧朝廷。」
units.en: When he took leave of Shikai, Shikai said, "You have been given a post that speaks for itself; to make a Yuan boy chancellor and vice chancellor is a deep shame to the court."
units.literal: Taking leave of Shikai, Shikai said: "The post you received is fair ground; to make a Yuan-family lad chancellor-in-chief deeply shames the court."

units.zh: 旣言而悔，仍執手慰勉之。
units.en: Having said it, he regretted his words and still took Wenyao's hand in consolation.
units.literal: Having spoken, he regretted it and still took Wenyao's hand in consolation.

units.zh: 猶慮文遙自疑，用其子行恭為尚書郎，以慰其心。
units.en: Still fearing Wenyao would doubt him, he appointed Wenyao's son Xinggong as a masters of writing lang to set his mind at ease.
units.literal: Still fearing Wenyao's self-doubt, he employed his son Xinggong as Masters of Writing lang to comfort his heart.

units.zh: 士開死，自東徐州刺史徵入朝，竟不用，卒。
units.en: After Shikai died he was summoned from governor of Eastern Xuzhou to court, but was never used and died.
units.literal: When Shikai died, summoned from Governor of Eastern Xuzhou to court, he was ultimately not employed and died.

units.zh: 行恭美姿貌，有父風，兼俊才，位中書舍人，待詔文林館。
units.en: Xinggong was handsome, had his father's bearing, and was gifted besides. He reached secretariat drafting officer and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
units.literal: Xinggong had beautiful appearance, his father's manner, and moreover brilliant talent; he reached Secretariat Drafting Officer, awaiting edicts at the Wenlin Hall.

units.zh: 齊亡，陽休之等十八人同入關，稍遷司勳下大夫。
units.en: When Qi fell, Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others entered the passes together with him. He rose gradually to lower grand master in the bureau of merits.
units.literal: When Qi perished, Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others entered the passes together; he was gradually promoted to Lower Grand Master in the Bureau of Merits.

units.zh: 隋開皇中，位尚書郎，坐事徙瓜州而卒。
units.en: Under Sui's Kaihuang reign he became a masters of writing lang; for an offense he was banished to Guazhou and died there.
units.literal: In Kaihuang of Sui he reached Masters of Writing lang; on account of offense he was banished to Guazhou and died.

units.zh: 行恭少頗驕恣，文遙令與范陽盧思道交遊。
units.en: Xinggong was rather proud in youth; Wenyao had him keep company with Lu Sidao of Fanyang.
units.literal: Xinggong in youth was rather proud and self-willed; Wenyao had him associate with Lu Sidao of Fanyang.

units.zh: 文遙嘗謂思道云：「小兒比日微有所知，是大弟之力，然白擲劇飲，甚得師風。」
units.en: Wenyao once told Sidao, "The boy has learned a little lately—your doing as elder brother; but his dice-playing and hard drinking are very much in your master's style."
units.literal: Wenyao once told Sidao: "The boy lately knows a little—this is elder brother's doing; yet his white-dice gambling and heavy drinking very much take the master's style."

units.zh: 思道答云：「郎辭情俊邁，自是克荷堂構，而白擲劇飲，亦天性所得。」
units.en: Sidao answered, "Your son's eloquence is sharp and lofty—he can surely uphold the family hall; but dice and deep cups are also his nature."
units.literal: Sidao answered: "Your son's rhetoric is lofty and sharp—he can surely bear the hall's beam; yet white-dice gambling and heavy drinking are also gifts of nature."

units.zh: 行恭弟行如，亦聰慧早成，武平末，任著作佐郎。
units.en: Xing Gong's younger brother Xing Ru was clever and precocious too; late in Wuping he served as an assistant in the Writings Office.
units.literal: Xing Gong's younger brother Xing Ru was also clever and precocious; late in Wuping he was appointed assistant in the Writings Office.

units.zh: 趙彥深，自云南陽宛人，漢太傅熹之後。
units.en: Zhao Yanshen came from Wan in Nanyang, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Zhao Xi.
units.literal: Zhao Yanshen was a man of Wan in Nanyang, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Xi.

units.zh: 高祖父難，為清河太守，有惠政，遂家焉，清河後改為平原，故為平原人也。
units.en: His great-grandfather Nan had been prefect of Qinghe; his fair rule made the family settle there. Qinghe was later renamed Pingyuan, so they counted as men of Pingyuan.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Nan was prefect of Qinghe; his kindly governance made the family settle there; Qinghe was later changed to Pingyuan, so he was reckoned a man of Pingyuan.

units.zh: 本名隱，避齊廟諱，改以字行。
units.en: His original name was Yin; to avoid the Qi temple taboo he went by his courtesy name instead.
units.literal: His original name was Yin; to avoid the Qi temple taboo he took his courtesy name as his public name.

units.zh: 父奉伯，仕魏位中書舍人、行洛陽令。
units.en: His father Fengbo had served Wei as secretariat gentleman and acting magistrate of Luoyang.
units.literal: His father Fengbo held office in Wei as secretariat gentleman and acting magistrate of Luoyang.

units.zh: 彥深貴，贈司空。
units.en: Once Yanshen rose to prominence, Fengbo was posthumously made minister of works.
units.literal: When Yanshen became eminent, [Fengbo] was posthumously invested as minister of works.

units.zh: 彥深幼孤貧，事母甚孝。
units.en: Yanshen lost his father early and grew up poor, yet served his mother with fierce devotion.
units.literal: Yanshen was orphaned young and poor, and served his mother with extreme filial piety.

units.zh: 年十歲，曾候司徒崔光。
units.en: At ten he once called on Minister over the Masses Cui Guang.
units.literal: At age ten he once called on Minister over the Masses Cui Guang.

units.zh: 光謂賓客曰：「古人觀眸子以知人，此人當必遠至。」
units.en: Guang told the guests, "The ancients read the whites of the eyes to know a man — this boy will go far."
units.literal: Guang said to the guests: "The ancients read the whites of the eyes to know men — this one will surely go far."

units.zh: 性聰敏，善書計，安閑樂道，不雜交遊，為雅論所歸服。
units.en: He was bright and quick by nature, skilled at writing and reckoning, easy in manner and devoted to the Way, and kept out of casual company — men of taste deferred to him.
units.literal: By nature he was intelligent and quick, skilled at writing and reckoning, peaceful and devoted to the Way, not mingling in social rounds — refined opinionists looked up to him.

units.zh: 昧爽，輒自掃門外，不使人見，率以為常。
units.en: Each dawn he swept outside the gate himself and would not let others watch — he made it a daily habit.
units.literal: At daybreak he would sweep outside the gate himself, not letting others see — he made it his constant habit.

units.zh: 初為尚書令司馬子如賤客，供寫書。
units.en: At first he was a lowly guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, hired to copy documents.
units.literal: At first he was a menial guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, supplying copy work.

units.zh: 子如善其無誤，欲將入觀省舍。
units.en: Ziru was pleased that he never erred and meant to bring him inside to see the offices.
units.literal: Ziru was pleased that he made no mistakes and wanted to bring him in to view the administration quarters.

units.zh: 隱靴無氊，衣帽穿弊，子如給之。
units.en: Yin wore unlined boots and threadbare hat and clothes; Ziru furnished him.
units.literal: Yin wore boots without felt lining, hat and clothes worn and tattered — Ziru supplied him.

units.zh: 用為書令史，月餘，補正令史。
units.en: He was made a secretariat clerical officer and, after a month, promoted to regular clerical officer.
units.literal: He was employed as a clerical officer in the secretariat, and after a month was promoted to regular clerical officer.

units.zh: 神武在晉陽，索二史，子如舉彥深。
units.en: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.
units.literal: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.

units.zh: 後拜子如開府參軍，超拜水部郎。
units.en: Later he was made Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, then leap-promoted to director of the water section.
units.literal: Later he was appointed Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, and was leap-promoted to director of the water section.

units.zh: 及文襄為尚書令攝選，沙汰諸曹郎，彥深以地寒被出為滄州別駕，辭不行。
units.en: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and took charge of selection, he culled the bureau directors. Yanshen, judged too humble in origin, was sent out as administrator in support of Cangzhou; he declined and would not go.
units.literal: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and oversaw selection, he culled the various bureau directors — Yanshen, because of low birth, was dismissed to be Administrator in Support of Cangzhou, and he declined and did not go.

units.zh: 子如言於神武，徵補大丞相功曹參軍，專掌機密，文翰多出其手，稱為敏給。
units.en: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; Yanshen was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, handling secrets alone. Most papers passed through his hand, and men called him quick and sure.
units.literal: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; he was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, exclusively handling secrets; most documents came from his hand, and he was called quick and responsive.

units.zh: 神武曾與對坐，遣造軍令，以手捫其額曰：「若天假卿年，必大有所至。」
units.en: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered a military command drafted; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said, "If Heaven grants you years, you will go far."
units.literal: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered him to draft a military command; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said: "If Heaven grants you years, you will surely reach great heights."

units.zh: 每謂司徒孫騰曰：「彥深小心恭慎，曠古絕倫。」
units.en: He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng, "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."
units.literal: He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng: "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."

units.zh: 及神武崩，秘喪事，文襄慮河南有變，仍自巡撫，乃委彥深後事，轉大行臺都官郎中。
units.en: When Gao Huan died the mourning was kept secret. Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect in person, leaving the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.
units.literal: When Gao Huan died they concealed the mourning; Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect on his own, entrusting the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.

units.zh: 臨發，握手泣曰：「以母弟相托，幸得此心。」
units.en: As he was leaving he clasped Yanshen's hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — trust that my heart is with you."
units.literal: When about to depart he clasped hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — may I have this heart."

units.zh: 旣而內外寧靜，彥深之力。
units.en: Inside and outside thereupon grew quiet — Yanshen's doing.
units.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were quiet — Yanshen's doing.

units.zh: 及還發喪，深加褒美，乃披郡縣簿為選，封安國縣伯。
units.en: When he returned to announce the mourning he praised Yanshen at length, opened the commandery-and-county register for selection, and enfeoffed him as baron of Anguo county.
units.literal: When [Gao Cheng] returned to announce the mourning he praised him greatly, opened the register of commanderies and counties for selections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anguo county.

units.zh: 從征潁川，時引水灌城，城雉將沒，西魏將王思政猶欲死戰。
units.en: On the Yingchuan campaign they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon go under, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still meant to fight to the death.
units.literal: On the campaign at Yingchuan they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon be submerged, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still wanted to fight to the death.

units.zh: 文襄令彥深單身入城告喻，卽日降之，便手牽思政出城。
units.en: Gao Cheng sent Yanshen into the city alone to persuade them; that same day they surrendered, and he led Sizheng out by the hand.
units.literal: Gao Cheng ordered Yanshen to enter the city alone to persuade; that same day they surrendered, and he personally led Sizheng out by the hand.

units.zh: 先是，文襄謂彥深曰：「吾昨夜夢獵，遇一群豕，吾射盡獲之，獨一大豕不可得。
units.en: Earlier Gao Cheng had told Yanshen, "Last night I dreamed I was hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.
units.literal: Earlier, Gao Cheng had said to Yanshen: "Last night I dreamed of hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.

units.zh: 卿言當為吾取，須臾獲豕而進。」
units.en: You said you would take it for me — and in a moment you had the boar and came in."
units.literal: You said you would take it for me — in a moment you had the boar and came in."

units.zh: 至是，文襄笑曰：「夢驗矣。」
units.en: Now Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled."
units.literal: At this Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled."

units.zh: 卽解思政佩刀與彥深曰：「使卿常獲此利。」
units.en: He then took Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying, "May you always win such profit."
units.literal: Thereupon he removed Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying: "May you always win such profit."

units.zh: 文宣嗣位，仍典機密，進爵為侯。
units.en: When Wenxuan succeeded to the throne, Yanshen continued to handle confidential affairs and was advanced to marquis.
units.literal: When Wenxuan succeeded to the throne, he continued to manage confidential affairs and was advanced in rank to marquis.

units.zh: 天保初，累遷秘書監。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianbao, he received successive promotions and became director of the Palace Library.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was repeatedly promoted, reaching director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 以為忠謹，每郊廟，必令兼太僕卿，執御陪乘。
units.en: Regarded as loyal and cautious, he was always made acting minister coachman at suburban and ancestral temple sacrifices, holding the imperial reins and riding in attendance.
units.literal: Because he was considered loyal and cautious, at every suburban and ancestral temple sacrifice he was always made concurrent minister coachman, holding the imperial reins and accompanying the carriage.

units.zh: 轉大司農。
units.en: He was transferred to grand minister of agriculture.
units.literal: He was transferred to grand minister of agriculture.

units.zh: 帝或巡幸，卽輔贊太子，知後事。
units.en: Whenever the emperor went on progress, Yanshen assisted the heir apparent and managed the affairs left behind.
units.literal: Whenever the emperor went on progress, he assisted the heir apparent and managed affairs left behind.

units.zh: 出為東南道行臺尚書、徐州刺史，為政尚恩信，為吏人所懷，多所降下。
units.en: He was sent out as acting bureau master of the southeastern circuit and inspector of Xuzhou. His government valued kindness and trust, officials and people cherished him, and he often humbled himself before others.
units.literal: He went out as acting bureau master of the southeastern circuit and inspector of Xuzhou. In government he valued kindness and trust, was cherished by officials and people, and often lowered himself to others.

units.zh: 所營軍處，士庶追思，號趙行臺頓。
units.en: Wherever he had camped with the army, gentlemen and commoners remembered him afterward and called the sites Zhao Xingtai camps.
units.literal: Wherever he established military camps, gentlemen and commoners remembered him afterward and called the places Zhao Xingtai camps.

units.zh: 文宣璽書勞勉，徵為侍中，仍掌機密。
units.en: Wenxuan sent him a sealed letter of encouragement, summoned him as palace attendant, and kept him in charge of confidential affairs.
units.literal: Wenxuan sent a sealed letter of encouragement, summoned him as palace attendant, and still had him manage confidential affairs.

units.zh: 河清元年，進爵安樂公，累遷尚書左僕射、齊州大中正、監國史，遷尚書令，為特進，封宜陽王。
units.en: In the first year of Heqing, he was advanced to Duke of Anle. He rose successively to left vice director of the Masters of Writing, grand arbiter of Qizhou, and supervisor of state history, then became director of the Masters of Writing, received the rank of special advance, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Heqing, his rank was advanced to Duke of Anle; he was repeatedly promoted to left vice director of the Masters of Writing, grand arbiter of Qizhou, and supervisor of state history, then moved to director of the Masters of Writing, became special advance, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang.

units.zh: 武平二年拜司空，為祖珽所間，出為西兗州刺史。
units.en: In the second year of Wuping, he was appointed minister of works. After Zu Ting sowed estrangement against him, he was sent out as inspector of Western Yanzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Wuping he was appointed minister of works; after Zu Ting sowed estrangement against him, he was sent out as inspector of Western Yanzhou.

units.zh: 四年，徵為司空，轉司徒。
units.en: In the fourth year, he was summoned back as minister of works and then transferred to minister over the masses.
units.literal: In the fourth year, he was summoned as minister of works and transferred to minister over the masses.

units.zh: 丁母憂，尋起為本官。
units.en: When his mother died he entered mourning, but he was soon recalled to his former office.
units.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and soon was restored to his original office.

units.zh: 七年六月暴疾薨，時年七十。
units.en: In the sixth month of the seventh year, he died suddenly of illness at the age of seventy.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, he died suddenly of illness, at the age of seventy.

units.zh: 彥深歷事累朝，常參機近，溫柔謹慎，喜怒不形於色。
units.en: Yanshen served successive reigns, always near the inner counsel, gentle and cautious, never letting joy or anger show on his face.
units.literal: Yanshen served successive courts, constantly in close counsel, gentle and cautious, joy and anger never showing on his face.

units.zh: 自皇建以還，禮遇稍重，每有引見，或升御榻，常呼官號而不名也。
units.en: From Huangjian on his honors grew weightier; when summoned he might even mount the imperial couch, and the emperor often called him by office title rather than by name.
units.literal: From Huangjian onward his treatment grew somewhat heavier; whenever summoned he might ascend the imperial couch; he was often called by office title and not by personal name.

units.zh: 凡諸選舉，先令銓定，提獎人物，皆行業為先，輕薄之徒，弗之齒也。
units.en: In every appointment he weighed candidates first and promoted men of character; the frivolous never made his list.
units.literal: In all selections he would first weigh and fix the list, promoting persons by conduct first — the frivolous were never enrolled.

units.zh: 孝昭旣執朝權，群臣密多勸進，彥深獨不致言。
units.en: After Emperor Xiaozhao seized court power, many ministers privately urged him to take the throne; Yanshen alone kept silent.
units.literal: After Emperor Xiaozhao took hold of court power, many ministers privately urged accession; Yanshen alone did not speak.

units.zh: 孝昭嘗謂王晞云：「若言眾心皆謂天下有歸，何不見彥深有語？」
units.en: Xiaozhao once said to Wang Xi, "If men say all hearts agree the realm has found its lord, why have you never heard Yanshen say so?"
units.literal: Xiaozhao once said to Wang Xi: "If the crowd says everyone's heart agrees the empire has its destination, why have you never heard Yanshen say so?"

units.zh: 晞以告，彥深不獲已，陳請，其為時重如此。
units.en: Xi told Yanshen; unable to refuse further, Yanshen submitted a memorial urging accession — such was the weight he carried in his age.
units.literal: Xi told him; Yanshen could not refuse further and submitted a memorial urging it — such was how the times valued him.

units.zh: 常遜言恭己，未嘗以驕矜待物，所以或出或處，去而復還。
units.en: He was habitually yielding and restrained, never arrogant toward others — so he might leave office and be called back again.
units.literal: He was habitually yielding and self-restraining, never treating others with arrogance — hence he might leave office and return again.

units.zh: 母傅氏，雅有操識。
units.en: His mother, Lady Fu, was refined in conduct and judgment.
units.literal: His mother, née Fu, was refined in conduct and judgment.

units.zh: 彥深三歲，傅便孀居，家人欲以改適，自誓以死。
units.en: When Yanshen was three, Lady Fu was already a widow; the family wanted her to remarry, but she swore she would die first.
units.literal: When Yanshen was three, Fu was already a widow; the family wished her to remarry, but she swore she would die first.

units.zh: 彥深五歲，傅謂之曰：「家貧兒小，何以能濟？」
units.en: When Yanshen was five, Lady Fu said to him, "We are poor and you are small — how can we live?"
units.literal: When Yanshen was five, Fu said to him: "The house is poor and you are small — how can we get by?"

units.zh: 彥深泣而言曰：「若天哀矜，兒大當仰報。」
units.en: Yanshen wept and said, "If Heaven takes pity, when I am grown I shall repay you on my knees."
units.literal: Yanshen wept and said: "If Heaven pities us, when I grow up I shall repay you looking up."

units.zh: 傅感其意，對之流涕。
units.en: Lady Fu was moved by his words and wept with him.
units.literal: Fu was moved by his intent and wept facing him.

units.zh: 及彥深拜太常卿，還，不脫朝服，先入見母，跪陳幼小孤露，蒙訓得至於此。
units.en: When Yanshen was made grand master of ceremonies and returned, he did not change out of court dress but went first to his mother, knelt, and said that as a small orphan he had come to this only through her teaching.
units.literal: When Yanshen was appointed grand master of ceremonies and returned, he did not remove court dress but went first to see his mother, kneeling and stating that from childhood he was orphaned and exposed, yet through her instruction had come to this.

units.zh: 母子相泣久之，然後改服。
units.en: Mother and son wept together a long while before he changed his clothes.
units.literal: Mother and son wept together a long while, then only did he change clothes.

units.zh: 後為宜陽國太妃。
units.en: Later she was made grand princess dowager of Yiyang.
units.literal: Later she was made grand princess dowager of Yiyang.

units.zh: 彥深有七子，仲將知名。
units.en: Yanshen had seven sons; Zhongjiang was the one of note.
units.literal: Yanshen had seven sons; Zhongjiang was the notable one.

units.zh: 仲將，沉敏有父風，溫良恭儉，雖對妻子，亦未嘗怠慢，終日儼然。
units.en: Zhongjiang was deep and keen with his father's manner, warm, mild, respectful and thrifty — even with wife and children he never slackened, grave all day long.
units.literal: Zhongjiang was deep and keen with his father's air, warm, mild, respectful and thrifty — even toward wife and children he never slackened, solemn all day.

units.zh: 學涉群書，善草隸。
units.en: He read widely and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
units.literal: He studied widely among books and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

units.zh: 雖與弟書，書字楷正，云草不可不解，若施之於人，卽似相輕易，若與當家中卑幼，又恐其疑所在宜爾，是以必須隸筆。
units.en: Even in letters to his younger brothers he wrote in proper regular script. He said cursive must be mastered, yet to use it on others is to treat them lightly; with juniors in the household one fears they will think that is simply how one should write to them — so the brush must be clerical.
units.literal: Though writing letters to his younger brothers, the characters were in proper regular script; he said cursive cannot be left unlearned, but to use it on people is like slighting them lightly; yet with junior kin in the household one fears they will suspect one should naturally write that way — so one must use clerical script.

units.zh: 彥深乞轉以萬年縣子授之。
units.en: Yanshen asked that his own enfeoffment be transferred to make his son viscount of Wannian county.
units.literal: Yanshen begged transfer to grant his son the enfeoffment as viscount of Wannian county.

units.zh: 位給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。
units.en: He served as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
units.literal: He held posts as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

units.zh: 隋開皇中，位吏部郎，終於安州刺史。
units.en: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he was director of the personnel section and ended as governor of Anzhou.
units.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was director of the personnel section, and ended as governor of Anzhou.

units.zh: 齊朝宰相，善始令終唯彥深一人。
units.en: Among Northern Qi chancellors, only Yanshen began well and ended well.
units.literal: Among Northern Qi chancellors, only Yanshen began well and ended well.

units.zh: 然諷朝廷以子叔堅為中書侍郎，頗招物議。
units.en: Yet he pressed the court to make his son Shujian secretariat vice director, which drew sharp talk.
units.literal: Yet he urged the court to make his son Shujian secretariat vice director — this drew considerable talk.

units.zh: 時馮子琮子慈明、祖珽子君信並相繼居中書，故時語云：「馮、祖及趙，穢我鳳池。」
units.en: At the time Feng Zicong's son Ciming and Zu Ting's son Junxin took the secretariat in turn, so people said, "Feng, Zu, and Zhao — they're fouling the phoenix pool."
units.literal: At the time Feng Zicong's son Ciming and Zu Ting's son Junxin in succession held posts in the secretariat, so the saying ran: "Feng, Zu, and Zhao are befouling our phoenix pool."

units.zh: 然叔堅身材最劣。
units.en: Of the three, Shujian's looks were the worst.
units.literal: Yet Shujian's physique was the worst of all.

units.zh: 山提以五月至鄴，楊愔卽召太常卿邢卲、七兵尚書崔㥄悛、度支尚書陸操、詹事王昕、黃門侍郎陽休之、中書侍郎裴讓之等議撰儀注。
units.en: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned director of ceremonies Xing Shao, minister of the seven armies Cui Lingjun, minister of revenue Lu Cao, household mentor Wang Xin, yellow gate attendant Yang Xiuzhi, secretariat gentleman Pei Rangzhi, and others to draft the ritual regulations.
units.literal: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned Director of Ceremonies Xing Shao, Minister of the Seven Armies Cui Lingjun, Minister of Revenue Lu Cao, Household Mentor Wang Xin, Yellow Gate Attendant Yang Xiuzhi, Secretariat Gentleman Pei Rangzhi, and others to deliberate on drafting the ritual regulations.

units.zh: 崔暹，字季倫，博陵安平人，漢尚書寔之後也，世為北州著姓。
units.en: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han minister of works, and for generations a leading house of the northern provinces.
units.literal: Cui Xian, styled Jilun, was a man of Anping in Boling commandery, a descendant of Cui Shi, Han Minister of Works, and for generations a prominent clan of the northern provinces.

units.zh: 經古冢，榮宗謂舍人元行恭是誰冢，行恭戲之曰：「林宗冢。」
units.en: Passing a tomb, Rongzong asked whose it was; Xinggong jested, “Lin Zong’s.”
units.literal: Passing an ancient tomb, Rongzong asked the attendant Yuan Xinggong whose tomb it was; Xinggong jested, “Lin Zong’s tomb.”

units.zh: 復問林宗是誰，行恭曰：「郭元貞父。」
units.en: Asked who Lin Zong was, Xinggong said, “Guo Yuanzhen’s father.”
units.literal: He asked again who Lin Zong was; Xinggong said, “Guo Yuanzhen’s father.”

units.zh: 及七月，大誅元氏，自昭成已下並無遺焉。
units.en: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Emperor Zhaocheng down, none were spared.
units.literal: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Zhaocheng down, none were spared.

units.zh: 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶
units.en: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
units.literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

units.zh: 穰侯，昭王之舅也，權重於秦，威震鄰敵，有旦莫偃伏之愛，心不介然有間，然范雎起徒步，由異國，無雅信，開一朝之說，而穰侯就封。
units.en: Marquis Rang, uncle to King Zhao of Qin, dominated that state and awed its neighbors; he shared the king's pillow and board without a shadow between them—yet Fan Ju, a stranger on foot, won a single hearing and sent Rang packing to his domain.
units.literal: Marquis Rang was King Zhao of Qin maternal uncle; his weight of power was in Qin, his awesomeness shook neighboring enemies; he had morning-and-evening couch-bending love, his mind was not stuck with a gap—yet Fan Ju rose from walking the roads, came from a different state, had no long-standing trust, opened one morning persuasion, and Marquis Rang went to his fief.

units.zh: 願將軍由周公之謙懼，損穰侯之威，放武安之欲，毋使范雎之徒得間其說。」
units.en: I urge you to keep the Duke of Zhou's humility, shed Marquis Rang's arrogance, and curb the appetites that ruined the Marquis of Wu'an—lest another Fan Ju find a crack through which to speak."
units.literal: I wish the general would take the Duke of Zhou humble fear, diminish Marquis Rang awesomeness, release the Marquis of Wu an desires, and not let a Fan Ju class obtain a gap for his persuasion."

units.zh: 李渾 子湛 渾弟繪 族子公緒 李璵 弟瑾 族弟曉 鄭述祖 子元德
units.en: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande
units.literal: Li Hun; his son Zhan; Hun's brother Hui; clansman Gongxu; Li Yu; brother Jin; clansman Xiao; Zheng Shuzu; son Yuande

units.zh: 繪，字敬文。
units.en: Hui, styled Jingwen.
units.literal: Hui, styled Jingwen.

units.zh: 贈南青州刺史，謚曰景。
units.en: He was posthumously made governor of Southern Qingzhou; his posthumous title was Jing.
units.literal: He was posthumously made governor of Southern Qingzhou; his posthumous title was Jing.

units.zh: 齊王蕭寶夤引為主簿記室，專管表檄，待以賓友之禮。
units.en: Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin brought him in as chief clerk and recorder, put him in charge of memorials and proclamations, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend.
units.literal: Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin brought him in as chief clerk and recorder, put him in charge of memorials and proclamations, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest and friend.

units.zh: 天平初，世宗用為丞相司馬。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Cheng employed him as staff officer to the chancellor.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, Gao Cheng employed him as staff officer to the chancellor.

units.zh: 使還，拜平南將軍、高陽內史。
units.en: On his return he was appointed general who pacifies the south and inner administrator of Gaoyang.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed general who pacifies the south and inner administrator of Gaoyang.

units.zh: 天保初，為司徒右長史。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianbao he was chief clerk on the right of the Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was chief clerk on the right of the Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 武定初，兼常侍，為聘梁使主。
units.en: At the beginning of Wuding he was concurrent regular attendant and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was concurrent regular attendant and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.

units.zh: 時勑侍中西河王、秘書監常景選儒學十人緝撰五禮，繪與太原王乂同掌軍禮。
units.en: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince of Xihe and Secretary Director Chang Jing select ten Confucian scholars to compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.
units.literal: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince Xihe of the Western River, Secretary Director Chang Jing, and ten Confucian scholars compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.

units.zh: 魏靜帝於顯陽殿講《孝經》、《禮記》，繪與從弟騫、裴伯茂、魏收、盧元明等俱為錄議。
units.en: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.
units.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites at the Xianyang Hall; Hui and his cousin Qian, Pei Bomo, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others were all recorders and discussants.

units.zh: 素長筆札，尤能傳受，緝綴詞議，簡舉可觀。
units.en: He had long excelled at letters; he was especially able to transmit and receive; in compiling and stitching together discussions, his selections were worth viewing.
units.literal: He had long excelled at letters; he was especially able to transmit and receive; in compiling and stitching together discussions, his selections were worth viewing.

units.zh: 年六歲，便自願入學，家人偶以年俗忌，約而弗許。
units.en: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.
units.literal: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.

units.zh: 伺其伯姊筆牘之間，而輒竊用，未幾遂通《急就章》。
units.en: He watched his elder cousin sister between brush and inkstone and would steal use of them; before long he had mastered the Jijiuzhang.
units.literal: He watched his elder cousin sister between brush and inkstone and would steal use of them; before long he had mastered the Jijiuzhang.

units.zh: 司徒高邕辟為從事中郎，徵至洛。
units.en: Grand Secretary Gao Yong summoned him as attendant gentleman; he was called to Luoyang.
units.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Yong summoned him as attendant gentleman; he was called to Luoyang.

units.zh: 卒。
units.en: He died.
units.literal: He died.

units.zh: 前後行人，皆通啟求市，繪獨守清尚，梁人重其廉潔。
units.en: Envoys who came before and after all sent letters opening relations and seeking trade; Hui alone kept to purity and loftiness — the men of Liang respected his integrity.
units.literal: Envoys who came before and after all sent letters opening relations and seeking trade; Hui alone kept to purity and loftiness — the men of Liang respected his integrity.

units.zh: 繪質性方重，未嘗趨事權勢，以此久而屈沈。
units.en: Hui's nature was square and weighty; he never hurried to serve the powerful — for this reason he long remained suppressed and obscure.
units.literal: Hui's nature was square and weighty; he never hurried to serve the powerful — for this reason he long remained suppressed and obscure.

units.zh: 繪曰：「今在晉陽，肅遏邊寇。」
units.en: Hui said, "He is now at Jinyang, sternly repelling border raiders."
units.literal: Hui said: "He is now at Jinyang, sternly repelling border raiders."

units.zh: 繪曰：「黑獺遊魂關右，人神厭毒，連歲凶災，百姓懷土。
units.en: Hui said, "Black Badger is a stray spirit in the west, loathed by men and spirits alike; year after year brings fierce calamity and the people yearn for their homeland.
units.literal: Hui said: "Black Badger is a stray spirit in the west, loathed by men and spirits alike; year after year brings fierce calamity and the people yearn for their homeland.

units.zh: 丞相奇略不世，畜銳觀釁，攻昧取亡，勢必不遠。」
units.en: The chancellor's stratagems are unmatched in the age; he gathers sharp blades and watches for an opening — attacking the benighted to take the doomed — victory cannot be far."
units.literal: The chancellor's stratagems are unmatched in the age; he gathers sharp blades and watches for an opening — attacking the benighted to take the doomed — victory cannot be far."

units.zh: 繪答書曰：「鴿有六翮，飛則沖天，麋有四足，走便入海。
units.en: Hui replied in a letter, "The pigeon has six pinions — in flight it pierces the sky; the elk has four legs — in running it soon reaches the sea.
units.literal: Hui replied in a letter: "The pigeon has six pinions — in flight it pierces the sky; the elk has four legs — in running it soon reaches the sea.

units.zh: 下官膚體疏懶，手足遲鈍，不能逐飛追走，遠事佞人。」
units.en: This humble officer's flesh is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies or pursue what runs, and go far to serve a flatterer."
units.literal: This humble officer's flesh is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies or pursue what runs, and go far to serve a flatterer."

units.zh: 是時世宗使暹選司徒長史，暹薦繪，旣而不果，咸謂由此書。
units.en: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.
units.literal: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.

units.zh: 渾與弟繪、緯俱為聘梁使主，湛又為使副，是以趙郡人士，目為四使之門。
units.en: Hun and his brothers Hui and Wei had all been chief envoys on missions to Liang; Zhan again served as deputy envoy — hence men of Zhao commandery called them the Gate of Four Envoys.
units.literal: Hun and his brothers Hui and Wei had all been chief envoys on missions to Liang; Zhan again served as deputy envoy — hence men of Zhao commandery called them the Gate of Four Envoys.

units.zh: 河間邢晏，卽繪舅也，與繪清言，歎其高遠。
units.en: Xing Yan of Hejian — Hui's maternal uncle — conversed in pure talk with Hui and admired his loftiness.
units.literal: Xing Yan of Hejian — Hui's maternal uncle — conversed in pure talk with Hui and admired his loftiness.

units.zh: 梁武帝問繪：「高相今在何處？」
units.en: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Hui, "Where is Chancellor Gao now?"
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Hui: "Where is Chancellor Gao now?"

units.zh: 繪曰：「兄所出雖遠，當共車千秋分一字耳。」
units.en: Hui said, "Though what you issue from is remote, you should share one character with Che Qianqiu."
units.literal: Hui said: "Though what you issue from is remote, you should share one character with Che Qianqiu."

units.zh: 繪欲修檻，遂因鬬死。
units.en: Hui wished to build a cage-trap; the beast thereupon died in a fight.
units.literal: Hui wished to build a cage-trap; the beast thereupon died in a fight.

units.zh: 繪曰：「猛獸因鬥而斃，自是偶然，貪此為功，人將窺我。」
units.en: Hui said, "The fierce beast died fighting — that was mere chance; if I greedily claim it as merit, people will peer into me."
units.literal: Hui said: "The fierce beast died fighting — that was mere chance; if I greedily claim it as merit, people will peer into me."

units.zh: 河間守崔謀恃其弟暹勢，從繪乞麋角鴿羽。
units.en: Administrator of Hejian Cui Mou relied on the power of his younger brother Xian and begged from Hui elk horns and pigeon feathers.
units.literal: Administrator of Hejian Cui Mou relied on the power of his younger brother Xian and begged from Hui elk horns and pigeon feathers.

units.zh: 右丞相、長廣王湛研機測化，體道居宗，人雄之望，海內瞻仰，同胞共氣，家國所憑，可遣尚書左僕射、趙郡王叡喻旨，征王統茲大寶。
units.en: Prince Zhan of Changguang, right chancellor, understands hidden workings and change, embodies the Way, and stands foremost among the clan. The whole realm looks to him as a hero among men. Born of the same mother and sharing the same breath, he is the support of house and state. Send Prince Rui of Zhaojun, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, to convey my intent and summon him to take charge of the throne.
units.literal: The Right Chancellor, Prince Zhan of Changguang, studies subtle workings and fathoms transformation, embodies the Way and stands within the clan; as a hero among men, he is looked up to within the seas. Of the same womb and shared breath, he is one on whom house and state rely. The Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Rui of Zhaojun, may be sent to explain the intent and summon the prince to govern this great treasure.

units.zh: 趙郡王叡與厙狄顯安侍坐，帝曰：「須拔我同堂弟，顯安我親姑子，今序家人禮，除君臣之敬，可言我之不逮。」
units.en: Prince of Zhao Gao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were seated in attendance. The emperor said, "Xu Ba is my cousin; Xian'an is my aunt's son. Today we observe family etiquette and put aside the formalities of ruler and subject—you may tell me where I fall short."
units.literal: Prince of Zhao Rui and Kudi Xian'an were in attendance seated beside him. The Emperor said: "Xu Ba is my paternal cousin; Xian'an is the son of my paternal aunt. Today let us observe family rites and set aside the respect due between ruler and minister—you may speak of where I fall short.

units.zh: 武成崩，尊為皇太后，陸媼及和士開密謀殺趙郡王叡，出婁定遠、高文遙為刺史。
units.en: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.
units.literal: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.

units.zh: 蕭明 蕭祗 蕭退 蕭放 徐之才
units.en: Xiao Ming; Xiao Zhi; Xiao Tui; Xiao Fang; Xu Zhicai
units.literal: Xiao Ming; Xiao Zhi; Xiao Tui; Xiao Fang; Xu Zhicai

units.zh: 蕭明，蘭陵人，梁武帝長兄長沙王懿之子。
units.en: Xiao Ming was from Lanling, son of Prince of Changsha Yi, eldest brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
units.literal: Xiao Ming was a man of Lanling, son of Prince of Changsha Yi, the Liang emperor Wu's eldest brother's son.

units.zh: 少歷顯職，封湞陽侯。
units.en: In youth he held eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang.
units.literal: In youth he passed through eminent offices and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang.

units.zh: 冬，霸先襲殺僧辯，復立方智，以明為太傅、建安王。
units.en: In winter Baxian attacked and killed Sengbian, restored Fang Zhi, and made Ming grand tutor and Prince of Jian'an.
units.literal: In winter Baxian attacked and killed Sengbian, restored Fang Zhi, and made Ming grand tutor and Prince of Jian'an.

units.zh: 九年二月，自湓城濟江，三月，卽帝位於郢州，年號天啟，王琳總其軍國，追諡明曰閔皇帝。
units.en: In the second month of the ninth year he crossed the river from Pencheng; in the third month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi; Wang Lin directed state and army; posthumous title for Ming was Emperor Min.
units.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he crossed the river from Pencheng; in the third month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi; Wang Lin directed state and army; posthumous title for Ming was Emperor Min.

units.zh: 天保六年，梁元為西魏所滅，顯祖詔立明為梁主，前所獲梁將湛海珍等皆聽從明歸，令上黨王渙率衆以送。
units.en: In the sixth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was destroyed by Western Wei, Gao Yang issued an edict installing Ming as Liang ruler; Liang generals previously captured, such as Zhan Haizhen, were all allowed to follow Ming home, and Prince of Shangdang Huan was ordered to lead troops to escort them.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was destroyed by Western Wei, Gao Yang issued an edict installing Ming as Liang ruler; Liang generals previously captured, such as Zhan Haizhen, were all allowed to follow Ming home, and Prince of Shangdang Huan was ordered to lead troops to escort them.

units.zh: 侍中裴英起衛送明入建鄴，遂稱尊號，改承聖四年為天成元年，大赦天下，宇文黑獺、賊詧等不在赦例。
units.en: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Cha, and the like were not within the amnesty.
units.literal: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Chao, and the like were not within the amnesty.

units.zh: 梁主旣納侯景，詔明率水陸諸軍趨彭城，大圖進取。
units.en: After the Liang ruler accepted Hou Jing, an edict ordered Ming to lead land and river forces toward Pengcheng for a major advance.
units.literal: After the Liang ruler had accepted Hou Jing, an edict ordered Ming to lead land and river forces toward Pengcheng, with a grand design of advance.

units.zh: 太清中，以為豫州刺史。
units.en: During the Taiqing era he was made inspector of Yuzhou.
units.literal: In the Taiqing era he was made inspector of Yuzhou.

units.zh: 明上表遣第二息章馳到京都，拜謝宮闕。
units.en: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang hurrying to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
units.literal: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang hurrying to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.

units.zh: 明年，詔徵明。
units.en: The next year an edict summoned Ming.
units.literal: The next year an edict summoned Ming.

units.zh: 霸先猶稱藩，將遣使送明，會明疽發背死。
units.en: Baxian still styled himself vassal and was about to send envoys to deliver Ming, but Ming died of a carbuncle on his back.
units.literal: Baxian still styled himself vassal and was about to send envoys to deliver Ming, but Ming died of a carbuncle on his back.

units.zh: 明渡淮未幾，官軍破之，盡俘其衆。
units.en: Ming had crossed the Huai only a short while when the government army defeated him and took his entire force captive.
units.literal: Ming had crossed the Huai only a short while when the government army defeated him and took all his host captive.

units.zh: 世宗禮明甚重，謂之曰：「先王與梁主和好十有餘年，聞彼禮佛文，常雲奉為魏主，並及先王，此甚是梁主厚意。
units.en: Gao Cheng treated Ming with great courtesy and said to him, "The late king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; I heard that when he performed Buddhist rites he would say he did them for the Wei ruler and for the late king as well—this was truly the Liang ruler's great kindness.
units.literal: Gao Cheng treated Ming with great courtesy and said to him: "The late king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; I heard that when he performed Buddhist rites he would say he did them for the Wei ruler and for the late king as well—this was truly the Liang ruler's great kindness.

units.zh: 不謂一朝失信，致此紛擾。
units.en: Who would have thought that in a single morning faith would be broken and bring this turmoil.
units.literal: Who would have thought that in a single morning faith would be broken and bring this turmoil.

units.zh: 自出師薄伐，無戰不克，無城不陷，今自欲和，非是力屈。
units.en: Since our armies went forth on a light campaign, there has been no battle we did not win, no city we did not take; now that we ourselves wish peace, it is not because our strength is spent.
units.literal: Since our armies went forth on a light campaign, there has been no battle we did not win, no city we did not take; now that we ourselves wish peace, it is not because our strength is spent.

units.zh: 境上之事，知非梁主本心，當是侯景違命扇動耳。
units.en: Matters on the border—I know they are not the Liang ruler's true intent; surely Hou Jing defied orders and stirred this up.
units.literal: Matters on the border—I know they are not the Liang ruler's true intent; surely Hou Jing defied orders and stirred this up.

units.zh: 侯可遣使諮論，若猶存先王分義，重成通和者，吾不必違先王之旨，侯及諸人並卽放還。」
units.en: You may send envoys to consult; if he still honors the late king's bond and restores friendly relations, I need not go against the late king's wish—you and the others will all be released at once."
units.literal: You may send envoys to consult; if he still honors the late king's bond and restores friendly relations, I need not go against the late king's wish—you and the others will all be released at once."

units.zh: 魏帝升門樓，親引見明及諸將帥，釋其禁，送於晉陽。
units.en: The Wei emperor ascended the gate tower, received Ming and the generals in person, released their bonds, and sent them to Jinyang.
units.literal: The Wei emperor ascended the gate tower and personally received Ming and the generals, released their bonds, and sent them to Jinyang.

units.zh: 於是使人以明書告梁主，梁主乃致書以慰世宗。
units.en: Thereupon he had men report to the Liang ruler with Ming's letter; the Liang ruler then sent a letter in reply to comfort Gao Cheng.
units.literal: Thereupon he had men report to the Liang ruler with Ming's letter; the Liang ruler then sent a letter in reply to comfort Gao Cheng.

units.zh: 上黨王進軍，明又與僧辯書，往復再三，陳禍福，僧辯初不納。
units.en: Prince of Shangdang advanced his army; Ming also exchanged letters with Sengbian back and forth several times, setting out fortune and calamity, but at first Sengbian would not accept him.
units.literal: Prince of Shangdang advanced his army; Ming also exchanged letters with Sengbian back and forth several times, setting out fortune and calamity, but at first Sengbian would not accept him.

units.zh: 旣而上黨王破東關，斬裴之橫，江表危懼，僧辯乃啟上黨求納明，遣舟艦迎接。
units.en: Then Prince of Shangdang broke Dongguan and beheaded Pei Zhiheng; the lands south of the Yangtze were gripped with fear, and Sengbian then memorialized Prince of Shangdang asking to admit Ming and sent warships to receive him.
units.literal: Then Prince of Shangdang broke Dongguan and beheaded Pei Zhiheng; the lands south of the Yangtze were gripped with fear, and Sengbian then memorialized Prince of Shangdang asking to admit Ming and sent warships to receive him.

units.zh: 王饗梁朝將士，及與明刑牲歃血，載書而盟。
units.en: The prince feasted Liang officers and men and, with Ming, slaughtered a victim and drank the blood, loading the covenant onto a chariot.
units.literal: The prince feasted Liang officers and men and, with Ming, slaughtered a victim and drank the blood, loading the covenant onto a chariot.

units.zh: 帝又密撰事條，將諫，其友王晞以為不可。
units.en: The prince secretly drew up a list of grievances and prepared to remonstrate, but his friend Wang Xi urged him not to.
units.literal: The Emperor also secretly drafted a list of matters and was about to remonstrate; his friend Wang Xi thought it inadvisable.

units.zh: 先是禁友王晞，乃捨之，令侍帝。
units.en: Wang Xi, his friend, had earlier been placed under restriction; now Emperor Wenxuan freed him and set him to wait on the prince.
units.literal: Earlier Wang Xi, his friend, had been confined; now he released him and ordered him to attend the Emperor.

units.zh: 又問王晞，晞答如顯安，皆從容受納。
units.en: He then questioned Wang Xi, who answered as Xian'an had; the emperor received all their remarks with composure.
units.literal: He again asked Wang Xi; Xi answered as Xian'an had, and all were calmly accepted.

units.zh: 尉瑾 馮子琮 赫連子悅 唐邕 白建
units.en: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian
units.literal: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian

units.zh: 馮子琮，信都人，北燕主馮跋之後也。
units.en: Feng Zicong came from Xindu and was descended from Northern Yan's ruler Feng Ba.
units.literal: Feng Zicong, a man of Xindu, was a descendant of Northern Yan's ruler Feng Ba.

units.zh: 子琮性聰敏，涉獵書傳。
units.en: Zicong was clever by nature and read widely in books and records.
units.literal: Zicong was clever by nature and ranged through books and records.

units.zh: 肅宗除領軍府法曹，典機密，攝庫部。
units.en: Gao Yan made him law staff in the general-in-chief's office, put him in charge of confidential affairs, and had him act in the treasury section.
units.literal: Gao Yan appointed him to the staff bureau for law in the general-in-chief's office, managing confidential affairs and acting in the treasury section.

units.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，領主衣都統。
units.en: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Chief Commander of Imperial Clothing.
units.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Chief Commander of Imperial Clothing.

units.zh: 至州未幾，太后為齊安王納子琮長女為妃，子琮因請假赴鄴，遂授吏部尚書。
units.en: Not long after he reached the province, the empress dowager took Zicong's eldest daughter as consort for Prince of Qi'an. Zicong asked leave to go to Ye and was then made minister of personnel.
units.literal: Not long after he reached the province, the empress dowager took Zicong's eldest daughter as consort for Prince of Qi'an; Zicong therefore asked leave to go to Ye and was then appointed minister of personnel.

units.zh: 俄遷尚書右僕射，仍攝選。
units.en: Before long he was promoted right vice director of the masters of writing and still acted in selection.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to right vice director of the masters of writing and still acted in selection.

units.zh: 世祖御正殿，謂子琮曰：「少君左右宜得正人，以卿心存正直，今以後事相委。」
units.en: Shizu sat in the main hall and told Zicong, "The young lord should have upright men around him. Because your heart is upright and true, I now entrust later affairs to you."
units.literal: Shizu sat in the main hall and said to Zicong, "The young lord should have upright men at his side. Because your heart is upright and true, I now entrust later affairs to you."

units.zh: 元文遙以子琮太后妹夫，恐其獎成太后干政，說趙郡王及士開出之，拜鄭州刺史，即令之任。
units.en: Yuan Wenyao, because Zicong was the empress's brother-in-law, feared he would encourage her to meddle in government. He persuaded Prince of Zhao commandery and He Shikai to send him out, made him governor of Zheng, and ordered him to take up the post at once.
units.literal: Yuan Wenyao, because Zicong was the empress's brother-in-law, feared he would encourage the empress to meddle in government; he persuaded Prince of Zhao commandery and He Shikai to send him out, appointed him governor of Zhengzhou, and ordered him to take up the post at once.

units.zh: 父靈紹，度支郎中。
units.en: His father Lingshao was a lang in the revenue section.
units.literal: His father Lingshao was a lang in the revenue section.

units.zh: 子琮妻，胡皇后妹也。
units.en: Zicong's wife was the Hu empress's younger sister.
units.literal: Zicong's wife was the younger sister of the Hu empress.

units.zh: 縱其子弟，官位不依倫次；
units.en: he indulged his sons and younger brothers, giving offices out of proper order;
units.literal: he indulged his sons and younger brothers, giving offices out of proper order;

units.zh: 世祖在晉陽，旣居舊殿，少帝未有別所，詔子琮監造大明宮。
units.en: When Shizu was at Jinyang, he occupied the old palace, while the young emperor had no separate residence, so he ordered Zicong to supervise construction of the Daming Palace.
units.literal: When Shizu was at Jinyang, he already occupied the old palace, and the young emperor had no separate quarters, so he ordered Zicong to supervise construction of the Daming Palace.

units.zh: 宮成，世祖親自巡幸，怪其不甚宏麗。
units.en: When the palace was completed, Shizu personally toured it and was surprised that it was not especially grand or splendid.
units.literal: When the palace was completed, Shizu personally toured it and wondered that it was not very grand and splendid.

units.zh: 子琮對曰：「至尊幼年，纂承大業，欲令敦行節儉，以示萬邦。
units.en: Zicong replied, "The sovereign is young and has inherited the great enterprise; I wanted him to practice sincere frugality as a model for the realm.
units.literal: Zicong replied, "The sovereign is young and has inherited the great enterprise; I wanted him to practice sincere frugality and show it to the ten thousand states.

units.zh: 兼此北連天闕，不宜過復崇峻。」
